title: Sep 26 Results + Sep 27 Preview: Nine Wins and a Solid Saturday
summary: Model hit 69.2% on Saturday with 9 wins. Mets-Nationals rematch tomorrow.

content.value:
## Another Winning Saturday in the Books

You know, after covering this game for as long as I have, a 9-4 day still gets the blood pumping. We hit 69.2% on Saturday's slate, and while it wasn't perfect—nothing ever is in this game—it's the kind of performance that reminds you why we trust the numbers over our gut.

## The Good, The Bad, and The Expected

The Dodgers took care of business in San Francisco at 63% confidence—that's the kind of pick that feels good from first pitch to final out. The Rays delivering at 61% against the Phillies? That's why you trust road dogs with the right matchup. Even saw the Rangers squeak one out at 51%, which is about as coin-flip as it gets, but we'll take it.

The misses? Well, the Nationals got us in the Mets game, the Jays couldn't hold serve against the Reds, and both the Guardians and Red Sox let us down. That's baseball. I've seen worse Saturdays turn into better Sundays.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Mets Get Another Shot

Here's what I love about this game—immediate redemption. The Mets couldn't get it done against the Nationals on Saturday, but Sunday brings a fresh matchup and a fresh opportunity. Sean Manaea gets the ball for New York against DJ Herz, and the model likes the Mets at 53%.

Now, 53% isn't screaming confidence, and I've been around long enough to know that any pick against a team that just beat you the day before requires a little extra faith. But Manaea's been solid down the stretch, and sometimes the best bet is on a good team bouncing back after a tough loss.

content.title: ⭐ Sunday's Top Pick
content.sub: Pick: Mets (53%) · Manaea vs Herz · Bounce-back spot for New York

content.value:
## The Sunday Outlook

Sunday baseball has a rhythm all its own. Day games, getaway games, bullpens stretched thin from Saturday's action. The teams that manage their energy best usually cash tickets. The Mets have been in these situations a thousand times, and with Manaea on the mound, they've got the right guy to settle things down.

I've seen this script before: good team loses a close one, comes back the next day focused and ready. That's what we're banking on tomorrow. Let's get back in the win column.

author: Max
